honesty.convention: these shapes are a convention this bundle invented, not a standard anyone else uses; the legend is in the wiki and on the page rather than assumed.
honesty.presentation_only: focus is presentation. Looking at a label changes nothing: no label is a score, none gates anything, and no grader reads which sign a learner faced.
honesty.provenance: a dashed outline on a SCHEMATIC sign and a solid accent on a RECORDED one restate the claim the registry behind them already makes - the label never upgrades a claim.
honesty.legibility: a label never shrinks below the declared floor while it is in range, carries a shadow so it survives a bright sky, and is drawn at device pixel ratio so it is not soft on a phone.
honesty.reduced_motion: viewers who ask for reduced motion keep the shapes and the colours and lose the easing: labels sit at full opacity rather than breathing as the head turns.
honesty.wayfinding: an exit chevron, a muster beacon and a door number are a reading of the floor plan this bundle drew, in a building that does not exist. They are training signage: not life-safety equipment, not an inspected route, not an approved sign, and not a substitute for the signs on the wall of the hall a learner is actually standing in.
honesty.identification: a door number and an asset tag are identifiers this bundle assigned, not numbers anybody else uses: they are derived from the hall, the room and the fixture that already exist in the registries, and they are set in mono because an identifier is a value a machine assigned, which is the rank this type scale already gives such things.
honesty.notices: a hazard notice states the condition the room's own conditions record holds. It does not classify, rate or permit anything, it cites nobody, and a space with no recorded condition gets no notice rather than one that says there is nothing to say.
honesty.no_marks: no sign in this world borrows a standards body, a standard's designation, a regulator or a real trade organisation: the shapes are this bundle's own convention and the words are plain practice, so nothing here can be mistaken for an inspected, approved or certified sign.
honesty.xr_panel: in a WebXR session the readout kind is reused for the wrist panel: one sign per dash gauge, drawn by the same label() the world signs use, off the same gauges() values the dash reads, with a warning readout wearing the crit accent the dash uses. Those signs ride the left controller (or hang ahead of the rig without one) at a fixed size and full opacity - they are on the hand, not in the world, so the view-direction scoring above does not apply to them. Verified against a mocked WebXR session only, never a physical headset.

no_marks.why: no sign in this world borrows a standards body, a standard's designation, a regulator or a real trade organisation: the shapes are this bundle's own convention and the words are plain practice, so nothing here can be mistaken for an inspected, approved or certified sign.

speech.draws: a rounded bubble with a tail pointing down at the speaker
speech.reads_as: somebody who will answer a question

tab.draws: a rounded plate with a downward pointer
tab.reads_as: a place you can go into

chip.reads_as: a thing you can open or pick up

plate.draws: a chamfered rectangle with a left accent stripe
plate.reads_as: a room, or a part of a place you are already in

pin.draws: a plate on a stem ending in a dot

banner.draws: a wide bar with a heavy left accent stripe

marquee.draws: a large plate with a rule above the title and letter-spaced caps
marquee.reads_as: the name of the whole place

ghost.draws: no plate at all - text with a shadow, so it does not compete with what it labels
ghost.reads_as: a detail, there if you look

readout.draws: a dark bordered box in monospace

chevron.draws: a plate whose leading edge runs out to a point, so the plate itself points the way
chevron.reads_as: the way out, and which way it runs

beacon.draws: a plate with a ringed dot struck at its leading end and the text set in after it
beacon.reads_as: a place to gather, marked so it can be found

stencil.draws: a hard-cornered square with a punched hole at its head and a heavy accent border
stencil.reads_as: the number a door answers to

tag.draws: a rectangle with its head corner cut away and an eyelet punched through it, like a tag wired to a machine
tag.reads_as: the identity of one piece of kit

notice.draws: a plate banded top and bottom with diagonal hatching in the accent colour
notice.reads_as: a condition in force in this space, not a name

ornaments.rule_under: a second rule under the title as well as over it, so the Academy's own marquee is not just a campus marquee with a different word on it

type.note: display for names, body for the line under them, mono for anything a machine measured - three faces, three ranks, and no fourth

campus.what: the name of a campus, over its plaza

district.what: a district of halls, over its block

hall.what: a hall you can walk into

advisor.what: somebody standing there who will answer questions

crib.what: a tool crib you can open

fixture.what: a bench or a piece of kit, named quietly

anchor.what: a real place, at its recorded distance and bearing

schematic.what: a drawn place - the dashed outline is the claim

route.what: a distance between two recorded points

readout.what: a measured number, from a seat or a chart

placard.what: what a room requires of you, read at its door

egress.what: the way out of a hall, read off the floor plan the bundle drew and pointing along it

muster.what: where a hall gathers when it empties, off the same plan the route is read from

door.what: the number a door answers to, derived from the hall and the room it opens into

asset.what: the identifier of one piece of kit, derived from its hall, its room and its place in them

hazard.what: a condition in force in a space, off the hazards its own conditions record already holds

focus.contract: each frame a label is scored 0..1 on the angle between the view direction and the label, inside the declared cone, and again on distance relative to how far out the view is; the two are multiplied. The score drives opacity (never below the floor while in range), size and tint, and it is eased rather than snapped so nothing flickers as the head turns.

screen.note: a fraction of viewport height, applied after the focus grow, so the clamp is what the eye finally sees

focus.focus_rule: the single most centred label within reach is the FOCUS: it takes the accent tint and lifts by lift_m, so a learner can see what they are about to act on without a cursor - which is what makes this work in a headset, where there is no cursor to have.
